open_points.subject: Model M15 — FlowEdge guard propagation
open_points.question: Which NodeExecution statuses make a source count as a "skipped node" for this rule: only `skipped_by_guard`, or also `upstream_failed` (or any non-executed source)?
options: Any source that did not execute causes downstream `skipped_by_guard`
open_points.default_guess: Only `skipped_by_guard` counts here; an `upstream_failed` source propagates `upstream_failed`.

open_points.subject: Model M15 — constant-fed input and node skipping
open_points.text: a port fed by a constant receives it and is never skipped
open_points.question: Does this exempt only that input port from causing `skipped_by_guard`, while another input port can still make the node `skipped_by_guard`, or does any constant-fed port prevent the whole node from being skipped?
options: Only the constant-fed port is satisfied; another unsatisfied input port can still skip the node
Any constant-fed input prevents the node from being `skipped_by_guard`
open_points.default_guess: Only the constant-fed port is satisfied; every other input port is evaluated independently.

open_points.subject: Model M15 — constant and edge targeting one input
open_points.text: a port fed by a constant receives it and is never skipped
open_points.question: May one input port be targeted by both a FlowConstant and one or more FlowEdges, and if so which source supplies its value and how do failure or guard outcomes on the edges affect the node?
options: The proof refuses any input port targeted by both a constant and an edge
The constant supplies the value and the edges are irrelevant to that port
The constant and edges may both deliver under a defined selection or combination rule
open_points.default_guess: The proof refuses an input port targeted by both a constant and an edge.

open_points.subject: Model M15 — precedence of upstream failure
open_points.question: What exactly makes `upstream_failed` applicable, especially when an edge from a failed upstream node is guarded and would otherwise be disabled: does any failed source connected to the node win, only a failed source on the affected input port, or only a failed source whose edge was required to deliver?
options: Any failed source connected to any input makes the node `upstream_failed`
A failed source on an affected input port makes the node `upstream_failed`, even if its edge's guard would disable it
Only failure of an edge that was required or enabled to deliver makes the node `upstream_failed`; irrelevant disabled edges do not
open_points.default_guess: Only failure on an edge that was required or enabled to deliver makes `upstream_failed` applicable; when that and guard-based exhaustion both apply, `upstream_failed` wins.
